feel.note: How the game feels: the timing and story-pacing numbers (tuning/01). Change a value here, not in a script; the scripts read them through G.feel("group.name"). Every entry has its value, its unit and what it does. Rule numbers (prices, weights, quality, growth ...) stay in the rule file of the system that owns them: the table 'Where to change a number' in docs/design/README.md says which.

pause.note: After a question, back on the farm: a fixed short pause before anything moves, the same after one question or eight.

rain.note: How long the rain shows, if it rained during the questions.

flick.note: How long the playback waits while plants flick through their stages and the bars pulse (three stages of stageSecs).

last.note: A last moment before the notes appear.

walkRight.note: A right answer on a walk (to the village, into or out of the forest): how long the green answer shows before the pop-up closes into the place.

stageSecs.note: How long each in-between stage of a plant shows on the map when it grew by more than one stage.

secs.note: How long a note (notification) stays on screen.

hintSecs.note: How long a hint stays (the short note when a bar is tapped).

newSecs.note: How long the 'New: ...' note stays when something new opens.

maxShown.note: At most this many notes at a time; the oldest one leaves first.

rationSteps.note: At most one story piece per this many Time Quiz questions.

barkRest.note: A bark (a short remark) does not come back within this many questions, unless the piece sets its own cooldown.

pictureHeight.note: How high a painted story picture is shown in the story box (the box is up to 760 wide).

newsMax.note: At most this many news boxes (a change of season, a golden acorn, a favour done, a party) wait for a quiet moment; the oldest goes.

walkMin.note: Rest: the farmer walks to the tent or house first; the window opens when he is at the door, but not before this.

walkMax.note: … and not later than this, so that a far walk does not make anyone wait (he is put at the door).

vanish.note: How long the farmer takes to disappear into the door before the Rest window opens.

inside.note: After the Rest window closes, he stays inside this long before he comes out again.

appear.note: How long he takes to appear at the door again.

stepOut.note: How far he walks out of the door after he has appeared (towards the player).

lockSeconds.note: How long the grown-up settings stay open after the lock was opened.

snowDepth.note: How far the winter snow caps reach down on roofs, tree tops and rails.

frostDepth.note: How far the winter frost reaches down on the top edge of the field patches and the road tiles (season-look/04).

frostStrength.note: How white that frost is: 1 is as white as the snow caps (season-look/04; the parent checks it in W9).

interruptions.note: What takes the screen next (interruption-queue): the interruption queue (kits/ui/interruptions.gd, set up in game/farm/ui/interrupts.gd) shows things that arrive on their own in this order, first wins. Each kind waits for the busy screens and the other kinds it names: a kind name means 'while one of that kind is waiting'. Busy screens: see 'busy'. Change the order or what a kind waits for here, not in a script.

busy.popup: A pop-up is open (Time Quiz, Rest, a card, a menu, or another interruption's box).
busy.playback: After the Time Quiz the farm has not started catching up yet (it still shows the old state).
busy.catchup: The farm is catching up after the Time Quiz (rain, plants growing, pests); ends when it has played to the end or a tap skipped it.
busy.sheet: A sheet over the farm is open (a station, the store, a place).
busy.bubble: A speech bubble (a bark) is on screen until it is tapped away.

order.note: The short notes kept for when a pop-up closes (a Rest medal …). They never hold the screen.
A postcard from a friend with a gift to pick. May come over a sheet.
The big 'New!' pop-up for a building, tool, Helper or perk. May come over a sheet.
A story Discovery: comes over a sheet (the child just tapped what it is about).
A story Scene (a delivery or favour handed over on the village square): comes over a sheet, right after the hand-over tap, before the square is left.
Every other story box (frame, beat, letter, moment, visit): waits until no sheet covers the farm.
A news box with a picture (a change of season, a golden acorn, a favour done, a party): the same quiet moment as a story box, after it.
A bark: a speech bubble; only one at a time, and it blocks nothing.
